They moved from Scarborough and depended on relatives in Chicago, Illinois; Croton-on-Hudson; [West De Pere, Wisconsin](/wiki/West_De_Pere,_Wisconsin "West De Pere, Wisconsin"); [Fort Wayne, Indiana](/wiki/Fort_Wayne,_Indiana "Fort Wayne, Indiana"); [Malden, Massachusetts](/wiki/Malden,_Massachusetts "Malden, Massachusetts"); and [Stratford, Connecticut](/wiki/Stratford,_Connecticut "Stratford, Connecticut").[[14]](#cite_note-14) When King was 11, his family moved to [Durham, Maine](/wiki/Durham,_Maine "Durham, Maine"), where his mother cared for her parents until their deaths. After that, she became a caregiver in a local residential facility for the mentally challenged.

King says he started writing when he was "about six or seven, just copying panels out of comic books and then making up my own stories ... Film was also a major influence. I loved the movies from the start. So when I started to write, I had a tendency to write in images because that was all I knew at the time."[[15]](#cite_note-:ParisReview-15) Regarding his interest in horror, he says "my childhood was pretty ordinary, except from a very early age, I wanted to be scared. I just did."[[16]](#cite_note-16) He recalls showing his mother a story he copied out of a comic book. She responded: "I bet you could do better. Write one of your own." He recalls "an immense feeling of *possibility* at the idea, as if I had been ushered into a vast building filled with closed doors and had been given the key to open any I liked."[[17]](#cite_note-17) King was a voracious reader in his youth: "I read everything from [Nancy Drew](/wiki/Nancy_Drew "Nancy Drew") to *[Psycho](/wiki/Psycho_(novel) "Psycho (novel)")*. My favorite was *[The Shrinking Man](/wiki/The_Shrinking_Man "The Shrinking Man")*, by [Richard Matheson](/wiki/Richard_Matheson "Richard Matheson")—I was 8 when I found that."[[18]](#cite_note-:ByTheBook-18)

King's aunt Gert paid him a [quarter](/wiki/Quarter_(United_States_coin) "Quarter (United States coin)") for every story he produced; his surviving earliest works include "[Jhonathan and the Witchs](/wiki/Jhonathan_and_the_Witchs "Jhonathan and the Witchs")", which he wrote at the age of nine.[[19]](#cite_note-WoodKing2012-19)

King asked a [bookmobile](/wiki/Bookmobile "Bookmobile") driver, "Do you have any stories about how kids really are?" She gave him a copy of *[Lord of the Flies](/wiki/Lord_of_the_Flies "Lord of the Flies")*, which proved formative: "It was, so far as I can remember, the first book with hands—strong ones that reached out of the pages and seized me by the throat. It said to me, 'This is not just entertainment; it's life or death.'... To me, *Lord of the Flies* has always represented what novels are *for,* why they are indispensable."[[20]](#cite_note-:LordOfTheFlies-20) He attended Durham Elementary School and entered [Lisbon High School](/wiki/Lisbon_High_School_(Maine) "Lisbon High School (Maine)") in [Lisbon Falls, Maine](/wiki/Lisbon_Falls,_Maine "Lisbon Falls, Maine"), in 1962.[[1]](#cite_note-OfficialBio-1) He contributed to *Dave's Rag*, the newspaper his brother printed with a [mimeograph machine](/wiki/Mimeograph_machine "Mimeograph machine"), and later sold stories to his friends. The **National Medal of Arts** is an award and title created by the [United States Congress](/wiki/United_States_Congress "United States Congress") in 1984, for the purpose of honoring [artists](/wiki/Artist "Artist") and [patrons](/wiki/Patronage "Patronage") of [the arts](/wiki/The_arts "The arts"). A prestigious American honor, it is the highest honor given to artists and arts patrons by the United States government. Nominations are submitted to the National Council on the Arts, the advisory committee of the [National Endowment for the Arts](/wiki/National_Endowment_for_the_Arts "National Endowment for the Arts") (NEA), who then submits its recommendations to the [White House](/wiki/White_House "White House") for the [President of the United States](/wiki/President_of_the_United_States "President of the United States") to award.[[1]](#cite_note-NEA_2018_Guide-1) The medal was designed for the NEA by sculptor [Robert Graham](/wiki/Robert_Graham_(sculptor) "Robert Graham (sculptor)").

In 1983, prior to the official establishment of the National Medal of Arts, through the [President's Committee on the Arts and Humanities](/wiki/President%27s_Committee_on_the_Arts_and_Humanities "President's Committee on the Arts and Humanities"), President [Ronald Reagan](/wiki/Ronald_Reagan "Ronald Reagan") awarded a medal to artists and arts patrons.[[2]](#cite_note-NMA_by_year-2)
